local_package.note: Read package metadata only. Matching public release source reviewed; binary reproducibility/commit identity not independently proved.

facts.finding: Select top-level model_provider = "openai" (or CLI -c model_provider='"openai"'). Omitted provider defaults to openai. Built-in OpenAI uses Responses and has supports_websockets=true; client prefers WebSocket while capability is true and session fallback is false. This selects WebSocket preference, not exclusive WebSocket enforcement.

[model_providers.openai].supports_websockets cannot explicitly change the built-in value. For key openai, merger applies only model_catalog_url and preserves built-in identity/inference/authentication. Other provider fields are discarded. Existing default remains true. Adding supports_websockets=true is redundant and must not be described as an effective override.

Keeping built-in openai preserves requires_openai_auth=true, unset provider base_url and auth-mode-based default URL selection. ChatGPT modes select CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL; other modes default to https://api.openai.com/v1. Existing explicit top-level openai_base_url is passed to built-in provider and must not be changed by this work.

No supported configuration setting for Responses WebSocket-only / disable HTTP fallback is present in full 0.169.0 config schema. Provider transport controls are supports_websockets and websocket_connect_timeout_ms; request_max_retries/stream_max_retries are retry budgets, not a fallback-off switch. Runtime fallback path is unconditional once selected.
features.responses_websockets and features.responses_websockets_v2 are Stage::Removed. Do not enable old flags as an attempted fix.

Fallback state is an in-memory session AtomicBool, initialized false in ModelClient::new and set true in force_http_fallback. Test explicitly proves stickiness across turns. Tests also verify immediate fallback on HTTP426 during startup prewarm and fallback after WebSocket retry exhaustion.

thread/resume first tries the already-loaded-thread path and reuses existing thread. A TUI reconnect or warm same-thread resume is not a guaranteed reconstruction of ModelClient and therefore does not clear sticky fallback.

inferences.finding: A truly fresh daemon followed by a cold resume of the same saved thread constructs a new session ModelClient with disable_websockets=false. Thus the old in-memory sticky fallback is cleared without deleting thread/history or changing auth. A genuine unloaded-and-cold thread reload has the same property.
inferences.limit: Source-derived inference; no daemon or TUI was restarted and no model request was sent.

inferences.finding: Fresh state only restores a WebSocket attempt/preference. Startup prewarm or later transport failure may immediately activate fallback again. Current responses_http telemetry alone does not establish why fallback began.

No code change can be replaced by unsupported flags to disable built-in fallback. If user requires fail-closed WS exclusively, stock supported configuration cannot promise that.

daemon_verb chooses restart for explicit --reload; otherwise no-backend start, same installed binary start/reuse, differing executable restart. Multiple or missing identity states are rejected (multiple is additionally rejected by ready_for_owner_reconnect before daemon_verb).

First ownership check, real-terminal requirement, per-slot native flock, second ownership check all run before computing daemon action and subprocess.run. Required endpoint validation and final ownership check precede execve.
